what: Replace prismis's per-topic vote model with carve-outs: repeated downvotes on items prismis matched to a category the user asked for carve a named, narrow slice out of that category (for example 'AI-agent incident news' inside 'LLM-driven security tools'), never lowering the category itself; the feature is opt-in or user-triggered, and every carve-out and its change over time is visible to the user without them having to manage it.
why: Today a vote is credited to the evaluator's own matched_interests, so a downvote that disputed one match on cerebro was learned as 'dislikes LLM-driven security tools' and dropped the user's core interests (unprioritized share ~55% to ~81%, issue #96). The vote model is now switched off (edc637a, [context] learn_from_votes) and the scores re-scored (f339776, 53% unprioritized afterwards), so votes are recorded and do nothing. Downvotes are a precision signal the user wants used: in rudy's words, 'its a precision metric and not meant to maintain the altitude of what I like but to carve out within those categories (if they were matched to what I dont want to see)'.
decided: A downvote is a precision signal against a match inside a category the user asked for; it carves a slice out of that category and never demotes, removes or dislikes the category itself.
One downvote is never enough: a carve-out needs more than one downvote in the same slice.
The feature is optional or user-triggered, not automatic by default.
The user can always see what has been carved out and how it changed over time, without having to manage it.
Votes stay recorded whatever the switch; nothing learned from votes reaches scoring while [context] learn_from_votes is off.
The re-score of the items scored under the poisoned preferences is done (cerebro, 1,918 items, 2026-10-15) and is not part of this work.
open: How is a carve-out represented and applied: as a deterministic step after the evaluator that demotes items close (by stored embedding) to the downvoted ones, as a natural-language exclusion line written into context.md under the category and read by the evaluator, or both?

What triggers a carve-out: a user-run command or TUI action that proposes carve-outs from accumulated downvotes for the user to accept (the shape of `:context suggest`), or an opt-in automatic step that applies them and records each change?
Where does the history of carve-outs live so the user can always see the changes over time: in context.md and its backups, in a record the daemon keeps, or surfaced in the TUI and web?
What counts as the same slice for the 'more than one downvote' rule: an embedding-similarity radius around downvoted items, the same matched category plus similarity, or a cluster a model names?
What happens to the current learned-preferences injection and the context auto-updater: are they removed, or kept behind learn_from_votes alongside the new mechanism?
Do upvotes play any part, given they mostly repeat High topics the user already wrote?
